clips.text: In normal sinus rhythm, the S A node initiates the rhythm, each visible sinus P wave is followed by a Q R S complex, and the P R relationship is consistent. The usual adult teaching rate is sixty to one hundred beats per minute. In lead two, P waves are typically upright and uniform. A narrow Q R S supports usual ventricular conduction. These electrical features do not guarantee normal cardiac output or exclude structural heart disease.

clips.text: Sinus bradycardia has sinus features at a rate below sixty beats per minute. A slower rate increases the time between beats, but its effect on output depends on stroke volume and the person's needs. It may occur normally during sleep or in well-conditioned people, or accompany medications and disease. Do not infer harm, safety, or a treatment choice from the rate label alone. First describe the rhythm and its measured features.

clips.text: Sinus tachycardia has sinus features at a rate above one hundred beats per minute. It may be an appropriate response to activity or stress, or accompany an underlying problem. At faster rates, diastole shortens and P waves can merge with preceding T waves. The source's usual ceiling of one hundred sixty is not a universal diagnostic limit. Rhythm identification depends on onset, P-wave features, and context, not a single maximum-rate rule.

clips.text: In respiratory sinus arrhythmia, sinus timing varies with breathing: heart rate usually increases during inspiration and decreases during expiration. P waves retain sinus features, and conduction to the ventricles remains consistent. This is common in healthy younger people. The changing R to R interval does not by itself indicate an ectopic rhythm. Compare the P waves and the repeating breathing-related pattern before naming the irregularity.

clips.text: A pause means an expected atrial activation is absent or delayed. Distinguishing sinus arrest from sinoatrial exit block requires attention to timing and the available tracing. A three-second cutoff alone does not reliably name the mechanism or prove that a pause is benign. A pause that is an exact multiple of the baseline P to P interval may support exit block in some patterns, but surface strips can be inconclusive. Describe the pause and any escape activity first.
